title: Chicken Pot Pie
subtitle: Deep-filled American comfort classic
excerpt: A deeply satisfying pie of shredded chicken, vegetables, and leeks in a creamy sauce, topped with a rough puff pastry lid and baked until golden. It is the kind of dish that feels impressive but is built on very simple techniques.
sourceNotes: Chicken pot pie is a cornerstone of American home cooking, with roots in European savoury pie traditions brought over by settlers. The defining characteristic is the thick, creamy filling sealed under a pastry lid and baked until the pastry is deeply golden.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked with the pastry lid on. Bake from frozen at 180C for 50 to 60 minutes until the filling is hot through and the pastry is golden.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept in the fridge. Top with pastry and bake when needed.

content.text: This recipe uses a rough puff pastry lid. To make it, combine 200g plain flour, 1 tsp salt, and 150g cold unsalted butter cut into cubes. Rub the butter very lightly into the flour so large flaky pieces remain, then add 3 to 4 tbsp ice-cold water to bring it together into a rough dough. Chill for 20 minutes before rolling out over the filling. The flakiness comes from leaving visible pieces of butter intact.

items.prepNote: poached in water or stock until cooked, then shredded

content.text: Make the rough puff pastry as described in the intro, form into a disc, wrap, and chill.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Cook the leek, carrot, and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until softened. Sprinkle in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Gradually add the stock and then the milk, stirring constantly until smooth. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the shredded chicken and frozen peas. Season generously. Remove the bay leaves and transfer the filling to the roasting tin.

Roll the chilled pastry out to just larger than the roasting tin. Lay it over the filling, pressing the edges to seal. Cut a couple of small slits in the top for steam to escape. Brush with a little milk to glaze.
Bake at 200C for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Pastry is soggy on the underside.
items.cause: The filling was too hot or too wet when the pastry went on.
items.fix: Cool filling slightly and ensure sauce is thick before topping.

items.symptom: Filling is too runny inside the pie.
items.cause: Not enough flour in the sauce, or milk was added too fast.
items.fix: Simmer filling sauce until noticeably thick before adding chicken.

items.cause: Oven temperature was uneven or pastry was not glazed.
items.fix: Brush pastry with milk and rotate the tin halfway through baking.
